READY / security PASS - final round under C34

The earlier pending lookup grants no new authority. Close still checks initial
ownership before pending_answer (crates/daemon/src/http/lifecycle.rs:496-514);
compact retains its existing target/identity/process/command validation before
the lookup (crates/daemon/src/http/mod.rs:2612-2675). The lookup reads/clones
pending metadata; it neither changes the original actor nor replaces the
held action.

PendingTurn retains the original closer, process identity and pane. A pending
close is acknowledged only for the same action, closer and incarnation
(crates/daemon/src/http/memory_turn.rs:429-448). Other requests are explicitly
refused rather than attached to an action that cannot execute them.
The refusal says the request will not run, tells the caller to ask again
after the turn and includes its deadline (:450-473).

The new why values are closed literals: another-action, another-closer,
another-incarnation. Structured details use the seat identity, action and
daemon deadline, not memory-note titles, close reasons or external message
bodies. Process identity and pane are compared, not exposed. The existing
caller derivation and original held-action authority/incarnation brakes remain.
No new secret, unsafe shell/path operation, or external-input exposure found.

Pending admission keeps the second comparison in hold for the race
(memory_turn.rs:305-307). The guard is dropped after proceed regardless of
closed/skipped/failed result (:335-349), and Drop removes the entry (:380-385).
The correctness role separately published PASS at this exact head and marked
R245-001 closed. No new C34 follow-up is required by this security delta review.

Cost: one additional request-driven in-process map lookup for close/compact;
no new recurring loop, timer, poll or process launch. The existing bounded
close retry remains at most five total attempts including current, pane_now
and CAS/receipt work. No live cost measurement is claimed.
